For planets with the same albedo orbiting the same star, equilibrium temperature scales with semimajor axis as

\[
T_{\rm eq}\propto a^{-1/2}.
\]

Thus,

\[
\frac{a_3}{a_1}
=\left(\frac{T_1}{T_2}\right)^2
 \left(\frac{T_2}{T_3}\right)^2
=(1.4)^2(2.3)^2
=(3.22)^2
\approx 10.37.
\]

Kepler’s third law gives \(P\propto a^{3/2}\), so

\[
\frac{P_3}{P_1}
=\left(\frac{a_3}{a_1}\right)^{3/2}
=(10.37)^{3/2}
\approx 33.4.
\]

The mass ratios and albedo value are not needed because the planets share the same host star and albedo.

Answer: D
